messages.content: What is Vault Genome?

Vault Genome is an AI continuity platform built on a frozen Producer/Verifier/Sealer interface that abstracts five Trusted Execution Environment backends: AWS Nitro Enclaves, Azure Confidential Computing with SGX, GCP Confidential VMs with SEV-SNP, Intel SGX bare metal, and a software simulator.
What does TAP V0.1 stand for?
TAP V0.1 is the TEE-Agnostic Attestation Protocol, an IETF-format draft RFC authored by the Vault Genome team that defines a uniform attestation surface across multiple TEE platforms.
What is the frozen interface in Vault Genome?

The frozen interface is three Go interfaces — Producer, Verifier, and Sealer — whose signatures cannot change without an explicit ADR amendment. Enforcement is done by an AST test in test/doctrine/invariants_test.go.
How does Vault Genome handle multi-TEE portability?

Vault Genome dispatches to one of five TEE backends based on a Provider configuration. Each backend implements the same frozen Producer/Verifier/Sealer contract, so callsites can swap from AWS Nitro to Azure SGX to GCP SEV-SNP without code changes.
What is the public conformance suite?

The public conformance suite is pkg/teeconformance, a Go package published under AGPL that any third party can run against their own TEE adapter to verify TAP-compliance. It contains 12 sub-tests including round-trip, replay rejection, evidence tampering, and sealing AAD binding.
What is the genome bundle format?

A genome bundle is a single file with magic bytes VG-GENOME-01, followed by a u32 big-endian metadata length, then JSON envelope metadata, then the AES-256-GCM sealed payload. The envelope carries the model snapshot description, the TEE measurement, the AAD, and provider-specific recovery parameters.
How does Vault Genome detect tampering?

Vault Genome uses AES-256-GCM with the payload SHA-256 bound as additional authenticated data. Any modification of the sealed bytes or the AAD causes the GCM authentication to fail, and acpctl genome open exits with code 4 without writing any files.
What patents has Vault Genome filed?

Vault Genome filed three USPTO Provisional Patent Applications on 2026-04-11. Specifications cover the TEE-agnostic abstraction with frozen interface, the multi-TEE Provider dispatch construction, and the multi-tenant HKDF key derivation for federated TEE deployments. Utility conversion deadline is 2027-04-11.
What is the AWS Nitro adapter?

The AWS Nitro adapter wraps Nitro Security Module attestation with AWS KMS sealing and COSE_Sign1 evidence framing. The Producer obtains a quote via /dev/nsm, the Sealer wraps the data key under a KMS CMK pinned to the expected PCR0, and the Verifier replays the COSE signature against the AWS Nitro root.
What is the Azure SGX adapter?

The Azure SGX adapter loads a signed enclave image, obtains DCAP attestation through the Microsoft Azure Attestation service, and seals data using SGX EREPORT-derived keys with a configurable MRENCLAVE or MRSIGNER policy. It runs on Azure DCsv3 confidential VMs.
What is the GCP SEV-SNP adapter?

The GCP SEV-SNP adapter consumes attestation reports from /dev/sev-guest on Google Cloud N2D Confidential VMs, validates AMD VCEK certificates against the AMD root of trust, and seals data using a key bound to the SEV measurement and guest policy.
What is the Intel SGX bare metal adapter?

The Intel SGX bare-metal adapter loads a .signed.so enclave image, performs DCAP attestation against the Intel SGX root, and supports an optional HSM wrap via PKCS#11 for hardware-rooted key custody on customer-controlled silicon.
What is the Simulated TEE backend?

The Simulated TEE is a software emulation that uses an in-process Ed25519 key for attestation and AES-256-GCM with a key derived deterministically from the workload measurement. It exists for CI, doctrine demos, and local development and must never be used in production.
How does measurement binding work in Vault Genome?

Each TEE Producer reports a 32-byte Measurement that summarises the workload identity. The Sealer derives its sealing key from this measurement, so unsealing requires a live TEE whose measurement matches the one recorded in the genome envelope. A divergent measurement is detected before AEAD even runs.
What is multi-tenant HKDF key derivation?

Multi-tenant HKDF derivation is a Vault Genome construction that derives per-tenant sealing keys from a single attested root key using HMAC-based key derivation with a tenant-scoped info string. Each tenant's keys are cryptographically independent, and the construction is the subject of one of Vault Genome's three USPTO PPAs.
What is the audit chain in Vault Genome?

The audit chain is a Merkle-linked sequence of AuditEvent records, each signed by the TEE attestation key. Every material event — seal, unseal, verify, recover, lineage — appends one record. Tip-hash continuity guarantees the chain is tamper-evident, and acpctl audit verify replays it end-to-end.
How do you reproduce the Vault Genome demo?

Visit https://vaultgenome.com/proof, download demo-genome.sh and the acpctl binary for your platform, install Ollama, pull llama3.2:3b, and run the script. Total time is about five minutes and every intermediate exit code is documented in README-reproduce.md.
What is acpctl genome seal?

acpctl genome seal reads an Ollama model from disk, packs its manifest and content-addressed blobs into a deterministic tar payload, seals the tar inside a TEE Sealer, and writes a single .genome bundle file containing magic bytes, JSON envelope metadata, and the sealed payload.
What is acpctl genome verify?

acpctl genome verify decodes a .genome bundle and validates the envelope structure. With --restored pointing at a target OLLAMA_MODELS directory, it re-hashes every blob on disk against the digest recorded in the envelope, proving bit-identical recovery.
How does Vault Genome relate to EU DORA?

EU DORA Article 28 mandates ICT third-party risk management for financial entities, including critical AI dependencies. Vault Genome's audit chain provides the exact evidentiary base regulators expect: hash-linked, signed, and recoverable for every material model change.
How does Vault Genome relate to the EU AI Act?

EU AI Act Article 16 requires post-market monitoring for high-risk AI systems with hardware-rooted attestation. Vault Genome's lineage tracing — from any inference back to the model genome ID, training data manifest, and sealed measurement — satisfies that obligation in a single command.
What does the SLSA L3 reproducible build give Vault Genome?

SLSA Level 3 reproducible builds mean two builds from the same commit produce byte-identical binaries, verified in CI. Combined with cosign keyless signatures and SPDX-2.3 SBOMs, this lets a verifier confirm provenance without trusting Vault Genome's CI infrastructure.
What is Generation in a Vault Genome bundle?

Generation is a monotonically increasing uint64 in the GenomeDescriptor that captures position in the succession chain. Generation 0 is the root baseline; each subsequent seal increments by one and links to its parent through a hash reference, building a tamper-evident timeline of model evolution.
What is acpctl genome chain?

acpctl genome chain walks a directory of .genome bundles, sorts them by generation, validates that every parent reference resolves to an existing bundle in the directory, and prints the lineage as a tree. It is the operational view of model evolution over time.
What is acpctl genome rewind?

acpctl genome rewind takes a generation number and a target directory, finds the matching bundle in the chain, and unseals it into the target — restoring the model to its exact state at that point in the timeline. The hash chain proves the restored state is the one that historically existed.
What is acpctl genome lineage?

acpctl genome lineage takes any bundle and walks the parent references back to the genesis bundle, printing every ancestor with its measurement and sealed-at timestamp. This is the lineage proof a regulator needs when auditing the provenance of an inference produced by a derived generation.
Is the Simulated TEE secure for production?

No. The Simulated TEE has no silicon root of trust — its sealing key is recoverable given the workload measurement, and its attestation key is an in-process Ed25519 keypair. It exists for local development, CI, and doctrine demos. Production deployments must use AWS Nitro, Azure SGX, GCP SEV-SNP, or Intel SGX behind the same frozen interface.
What does AGPL-3.0 mean for forks of Vault Genome?

AGPL-3.0 is a strong copyleft license: any party that distributes a modified version of Vault Genome — including running it as a network service — must publish their modifications under the same license. Vault Genome offers a commercial license for users who need to keep modifications private.
What is the Vault Genome reproducible-proof page?

The reproducible-proof page at https://vaultgenome.com/proof publishes downloadable artifacts so any visitor can reproduce the seal/restore/verify/tamper demo on their own laptop in five minutes — including a recorded asciinema cast, a bash runner, the acpctl binary for three platforms, and a README.
How does Vault Genome support time-travel recovery?

Time-travel recovery uses the chain of generation bundles. Each bundle captures a snapshot or delta at a specific moment, linked to its parent. acpctl genome rewind --to=N restores the model to its exact state at generation N, which is essential for regulator replay and root-cause analysis.
